confirmedGap.fact: Current handshake correctly validates outer ec, M2/np, decrypts bounded SPD and checks adsid/idms; it only recognizes outer complete.Status.au secondary state. An authenticated decrypted SPD409/url with no outer au currently goes toward sk/c and app-token requests instead of surfacing the supported 2FA challenge.

primaryContract.fact: The common operation decoder rejects outer Status.ec!=0 before decoding the authenticated complete body.

After M2 and negotiation verification, decrypt SPD, decode required integer status-code plus optional String url and LoginData, then409 triggers one secondary-auth cycle; a repeated409 on retry fails.

nil mode means auto-requested and only validateCode; trustedDevice mode makes its explicit request then validates. secondaryAuth uses SMS in upstream, including an unbound phone-ID assumption; this narrow app slice must keep SMS unsupported.

url is an auth-mode raw token, not a network destination. Upstream flatMap maps an unknown token to nil; root deliberately proposes a stricter bounded unsupported policy rather than copying that fallback.

Upstream decodes adsid/GsIdmsToken/sk/c before its409 branch. Current app secondary flow uses only authenticated bounded dsid/idms; no claim of complete upstream SPD schema parity is made by this pre-review.

recommendedOrdering: Keep the current HTTP/outer Status.ec failures authoritative before processing complete payload.
Keep bounded SPD/sc/M2/np parsing, M2 verification, negotiation MAC verification, decryption and strict plist parsing ahead of every new challenge classification or secondary HTTP side effect.

Parse only verified decrypted status-code as a strict integer when present. Distinguish absent status-code legacy compatibility from malformed String/Bool/Data values; do not confuse it with HTTP409 or outer ec.

On supported SPD409 classify explicit secondary mode before app-token exchange. nil/absent url returns pending challenge without another trusted-device request; supported trustedDevice token requests exactly once, then returns pending. Unknown/secondaryAuth/absolute URL/empty/nonString mode must stay typed unsupported or malformed and must never select host/path.
Carry the secondary mode explicitly through Handshake into signIn, preserving busy, in-memory expiry, cancellation checks, single-use pending consumption and existing fixed validate route.

After submitting a code repeat the complete authenticated SRP handshake; another secondary challenge fails through existing no-recursion behavior. Account connect/storage/team/signing authority are still reached only by a verified nonsecondary candidate and normal account validation.

signalConflictPolicyNotDefinedByPrimary.fact: The bound upstream five sources do not use outer au and do not define how it conflicts with SPD409/url. A conflict policy is therefore an app decision, not a proven Apple protocol fact.
signalConflictPolicyNotDefinedByPrimary.recommendation: Fail closed on contradictory or unknown simultaneous signals before requesting/validating a code. Keep outer trustedDevice legacy behavior when new SPD fields are absent; accept simultaneous SPD409 trustedDevice plus the same supported outer intent only when explicitly treated as consistent. Do not convert invalid mode to manual nil.

existingPublicFixtureInspection.performed: One read-only Python inspection decoded public vector JSON and AES-CBC SPD with its public K using the existing derivation; this did not execute Swift, old test suites, HTTP, Apple or authentication operations. existingPublicFixtureInspection.consequence: Do not require new SPD fields on existing legacy vectors. To cover409, generate actual re-encrypted SPD and matching np from independent public reference values; attaching fields outside authenticated ciphertext is not equivalent.

fixtureAttachmentPoints.fact: Existing serialized Mode/Peer.complete has exact init/M1 checks and bound M2/spd/sc/np. Add modes selecting sealed challenge vectors, then choose the original successful payload after validated=true.

Current trustedDevice method already verifies GET routes, security-code, identity-token, SRP restart, secure storage absent before completion and consumed challenge rejection. Add manual vector asserting exact path sequence omits trusteddevice, preserving old sequence.
Tampered M2 or np on a409 vector must fail before request, pending challenge, app-token or storage publication. Existing bad-proof modes and storage checks are real fixture seams.
Transport is the actual app URLSession implementation with synthetic URLProtocol peer and real Keychain storage/vault/account client. This is not actual Apple network/TLS or live account acceptance.
Keep actual cancellation, pending-clear and AppSession owner cleanup paths; do not silently catch failures or retry secondary requests in background.
